alex: Quick sync - proposing a lightweight degraded-mode contract for the API gateway when edge pools are saturated. Goal: allow conservative fallbacks (lower-tier model, cached partial, or short-circuit) while keeping semantics explicit for side-effecting routes. Thoughts?
maria: +1. Sketch the signal shape? header, trailer, or control channel?
alex: Two-part approach: immediate header that indicates permission for fallback, e.g. X-RW-Edge-Degrade: level=soft; allow-fallback=true; prefer=cache; and a final trailer X-RW-Edge-Outcome with values full|partial|fallback so clients can decide mid-stream.
ryan: Risk: surprising clients that expect strong semantics. Side-effects are dangerous if we silently fallback or hedge.
alex: Agreed. For side-effect routes gateway must refuse opaque fallbacks unless route opts in and request has Idempotency-Key. No resume for side-effecting ops.
linh: For cached partials we can stream cache tokens and include X-RW-Edge-Outcome: partial; cached=true trailer. Clients could surface "partial reply available" and optionally call a resume endpoint.
maria: Resume token UX: pros — resume to get higher fidelity; cons — token leakage and complexity.
alex: Proposal: opaque resume handle only if route allows resume and the origin model produced stable prefixes. Header X-RW-Resume-Handle: v1:base64...; opt-in per route.
ryan: Billing: need explicit billing tags emitted by gateway like edge_outcome=partial_cached or fallback_model=redwood-compact-v1 so billing and cost dashboards reflect real usage.
linh: SLOs: expose response_mode metric values normal|degraded|fallback|cached_partial so console rollups show degradation rates.
alex: Implementation sketch: ingress evaluates route policy (allowFallback, allowResume, sideEffectSafe). If pool saturated pick strategy based on prefer= header and route config. Attach immediate header to client e.g. X-RW-Edge-Degrade: active; strategy=fallback_model; fallback=redwood-compact-v1. Stream tokens; include X-RW-Edge-Outcome at end and X-RW-Resume-Handle if applicable.
maria: Hedging: only for read-only endpoints. Dedupe by request-id at app layer and never auto-retry side-effecting operations without Idempotency-Key. Bounded hedging window (e.g. 300ms) and cost-accounting.
linh: Trailers are not universal. Provide fallback: send X-RW-Edge-Outcome as trailer when supported, otherwise as final header before close. Also add consumer header Prefer: degrade=allow; fallback=cache,model so clients can request degradation.
ryan: Tests: integration test for side-effect routes ensuring gateway refuses fallback without Idempotency-Key and returns 503 with clear body and Retry-After where appropriate. Also add fidelity regression evals for routes that opt into fallback.
deploy-bot: canary:edge-degrade-v1 deployed to prod-canary (10% ingress) at 2026-03-23T15:12Z :rocket:
alex: Action items: alex -> draft RFC with header/trailer spec and curl examples; linh -> add metrics schema for response_mode, edge_outcome, fallback_model; ryan -> hazard checklist and tests for hedging/idempotency; maria -> experiment plan and eval prompt set. I'll open RFC PR this week.
maria: thanks, helpful framing.
ryan: +1.
linh: will add sample dashboards.
alex: will post RFC link when ready.
